title: Your Bills: NJ Rates Today
briefing: Today's grain: 0–3 posts may be forged. Your wallet, your watch.

posts.body: BPU President just confirmed: NO increase in electric rates. Screenshot this before they walk it back. #NJ #UtilityBills

quote.text: Taken together with the items on the agenda earlier this month, these actions will result in no increase in electricity rates and a slight decrease in gas rates.
quote.speaker: Ben Hertz-Shargel, the board's president

posts.body: New Jersey electricity bills jumped roughly 20 percent last year, driven in large part by rising costs in PJM's capacity market.

The Board of Public Utilities approved a series of rate changes Thursday that will keep rates roughly level for residential electric ratepayers while shaving dollars off most residential gas customers' monthly bills.

The average Rockland customer using about 650 kilowatt-hours within a billing cycle can expect their bill to decrease by 67 cents, board staff said, and ratepayers with Atlantic City Electric will pay 5 cents less each month.
The Board of Public Utilities on Thursday unanimously approved the launch of an interim virtual power plant program and the next phase of the state's energy storage program.
